questions.question: Describe the pathway of air from the nose to the alveoli.

points.text: Nose → Pharynx → Larynx → Trachea → Bronchi → Bronchioles → Alveoli. Each structure filters, warms or channels the air towards the alveoli where gaseous exchange occurs.

questions.question: Explain three features of alveoli that make them efficient for gaseous exchange.

points.text: Large surface area (approximately 70m²) allows a high rate of diffusion. Thin walls (one cell thick for both alveoli and capillaries) create a short diffusion distance. Moist lining allows gases to dissolve before diffusing. Dense capillary network maintains the concentration gradient with constant blood flow.

questions.question: Why does the left ventricle have a thicker muscular wall than the right ventricle?

points.text: The left ventricle pumps blood through the aorta to the entire body (systemic circulation), requiring high pressure. The right ventricle only pumps blood to the nearby lungs (pulmonary circulation), which requires much lower pressure.

questions.question: Describe the difference between pulmonary circulation and systemic circulation.

points.text: Pulmonary circulation carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs via the pulmonary artery, and returns oxygenated blood to the left atrium via the pulmonary vein. Systemic circulation carries oxygenated blood from the left ventricle to the body via the aorta, and returns deoxygenated blood to the right atrium via the vena cava.

questions.question: Compare the structure of arteries, veins and capillaries.

points.text: Arteries have thick walls (muscle and elastic tissue), small lumens and high pressure, with no valves. Veins have thinner walls, larger lumens and lower pressure, with valves to prevent backflow. Capillaries are one cell thick with very small lumens, allowing exchange of materials with tissues.

questions.question: Why do veins contain valves but arteries do not?

points.text: Veins carry blood at low pressure back to the heart. Without valves, gravity and low pressure would cause blood to pool or flow backwards, especially in the legs. Arteries carry blood at high pressure, generated by the heart, so the pressure itself prevents backflow and valves are unnecessary.
